title: What Happens When Your EV Hits 0%? 🔋🐢 #shorts

scenes.text: What really happens when your electric car hits zero percent?
It won't just die. The warnings get louder, then a turtle mode cuts your power and top speed.
There's usually a hidden buffer, too. In a AAA test, a Model 3 drove thirteen miles past zero.
When it finally stops, the small twelve volt battery still runs the locks and the hazard lights.
Then you need a flatbed. In most EVs the motor stays geared to the wheels, so towing on them turns it into a generator.
Roadside chargers help, slowly: about fourteen miles in thirty minutes in AAA's test.
That buffer protects the battery. It's not there to save your trip. Follow EV Drive.
